Question: Point \(P\) is outside circle \(C\) on the plane. At most how many points on \(C\) are \(3\) cm from \(P?\)
Solution:
All points \(3\) cm from \(P\) form a circle centered at \(P\) with radius \(3\) cm. The requested points are exactly the intersections of this circle with \(C\).

These circles are distinct: because \(P\) is outside \(C\), it cannot be the center of \(C\). Two distinct circles have at most two common points.

Two intersections are possible. For example, let \(C\) have radius \(2\) cm and let \(P\) be \(3\) cm from its center. Then \(P\) is outside \(C\), and the center distance satisfies
\[
|3-2|<3<3+2,
\]
so the two circles intersect twice. Therefore the maximum is \(\boxed{2}\), choice B.
